audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Exodus / Shemot covenant ordinances text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for restitution, theft, deposits, seduction, vulnerable persons, lending, firstfruits, holiness.

verses.restored: When a man steals ox or sheep and slaughters it or sells it, five cattle he shall repay for the ox, and four flock-animals for the sheep.

familiar.text: If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.

verses.restored: If thief is found breaking in and is struck and dies, there is no bloodguilt for him.

familiar.text: If a thief be found breaking up, and be smitten that he die, there shall no blood be shed for him.

verses.restored: If sun has risen upon him, there is bloodguilt for him. Repaying, he shall repay; if he has nothing, he shall be sold for his theft.

familiar.text: If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be blood shed for him; for he should make full restitution; if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.

verses.restored: If stolen thing is surely found alive in his hand, whether ox, donkey, or sheep, double he shall repay.

familiar.text: If the theft be certainly found in his hand alive, whether it be ox, or ass, or sheep; he shall restore double.

verses.restored: When a man causes field or vineyard to be grazed, and sends out his beast and it grazes in another's field, from best of his field and best of his vineyard he shall repay.

familiar.text: If a man shall cause a field or vineyard to be eaten, and shall put in his beast, and shall feed in another man’s field; of the best of his own field, and of the best of his own vineyard, shall he make restitution.

verses.restored: When fire goes out and finds thorns, and stacked grain or standing grain or field is consumed, repaying, the one kindling the fire shall repay.

familiar.text: If fire break out, and catch in thorns, so that the stacks of corn, or the standing corn, or the field, be consumed therewith; he that kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.

verses.restored: When a man gives to his companion silver or vessels to guard, and it is stolen from house of man, if thief is found, he shall repay double.

familiar.text: If a man shall deliver unto his neighbour money or stuff to keep, and it be stolen out of the man’s house; if the thief be found, let him pay double.

verses.restored: If thief is not found, owner of house shall come near to the Divine, to see whether he has stretched his hand against property of his companion.

familiar.text: If the thief be not found, then the master of the house shall be brought unto the judges, to see whether he have put his hand unto his neighbour’s goods.

verses.restored: For every matter of transgression, concerning ox, donkey, sheep, garment, every lost thing of which one says, This is it, the matter of both shall come to the Divine; whom Divine condemns shall repay double to his companion.

familiar.text: For all manner of trespass, whether it be for ox, for ass, for sheep, for raiment, or for any manner of lost thing, which another challengeth to be his, the cause of both parties shall come before the judges; and whom the judges shall condemn, he shall pay double unto his neighbour.

verses.restored: When a man gives to his companion donkey, ox, sheep, or any beast to guard, and it dies or is hurt or driven away with no one seeing,

familiar.text: If a man deliver unto his neighbour an ass, or an ox, or a sheep, or any beast, to keep; and it die, or be hurt, or driven away, no man seeing it:

verses.restored: oath of YHWH shall be between them, whether he stretched hand against property of his companion; its owner shall accept, and he shall not repay.

familiar.text: Then shall an oath of the LORD be between them both, that he hath not put his hand unto his neighbour’s goods; and the owner of it shall accept thereof, and he shall not make it good.

verses.restored: But if stealing, it was stolen from him, he shall repay to its owner.

familiar.text: And if it be stolen from him, he shall make restitution unto the owner thereof.

verses.restored: If tearing, it was torn, he shall bring it as witness; the torn thing he shall not repay.

familiar.text: If it be torn in pieces, then let him bring it for witness, and he shall not make good that which was torn.

verses.restored: When a man asks from his companion and it is hurt or dies, its owner not with it, repaying, he shall repay.

familiar.text: And if a man borrow ought of his neighbour, and it be hurt, or die, the owner thereof being not with it, he shall surely make it good.

verses.restored: If its owner is with it, he shall not repay; if it was hired, it came for its hire.

familiar.text: But if the owner thereof be with it, he shall not make it good: if it be an hired thing, it came for his hire.

verses.restored: When a man entices a virgin who is not betrothed and lies with her, bride-price he shall surely give for her to be his wife.

familiar.text: And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.

verses.restored: If her father utterly refuses to give her to him, he shall weigh silver according to bride-price of virgins.

familiar.text: If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.

verses.restored: You shall not let a sorceress live.

familiar.text: Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.

verses.restored: Anyone lying with a beast shall surely be put to death.

familiar.text: Whosoever lieth with a beast shall surely be put to death.

verses.restored: One sacrificing to gods, except to YHWH alone, shall be devoted to destruction.

familiar.text: He that sacrificeth unto any god, save unto the LORD only, he shall be utterly destroyed.

verses.restored: You shall not wrong a sojourner or oppress him, for you were sojourners in land of Egypt.

familiar.text: Thou shalt neither vex a stranger, nor oppress him: for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.

verses.restored: You shall not afflict any widow or orphan.

familiar.text: Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child.

verses.restored: If afflicting, you afflict them, and crying, they cry to me, hearing, I will hear their cry.

familiar.text: If thou afflict them in any wise, and they cry at all unto me, I will surely hear their cry;

verses.restored: My anger will burn, and I will kill you with sword, and your women shall become widows and your children orphans.

familiar.text: And my wrath shall wax hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.

verses.restored: If you lend silver to my people, to the poor with you, you shall not be to him as creditor; you shall not place interest upon him.

familiar.text: If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer, neither shalt thou lay upon him usury.

verses.restored: If taking pledge, you take your companion's cloak, before sun goes down you shall return it to him,

familiar.text: If thou at all take thy neighbour’s raiment to pledge, thou shalt deliver it unto him by that the sun goeth down:

verses.restored: for it is his only covering, his garment for his skin; in what shall he lie down? And it shall be, when he cries to me, I will hear, for I am gracious.

familiar.text: For that is his covering only, it is his raiment for his skin: wherein shall he sleep? and it shall come to pass, when he crieth unto me, that I will hear; for I am gracious.

verses.restored: You shall not curse Divine, and a leader among your people you shall not curse.

familiar.text: Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people.

verses.restored: Your fullness and your outflow you shall not delay. Firstborn of your sons you shall give to me.

familiar.text: Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits, and of thy liquors: the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me.

verses.restored: Thus you shall do with your ox and your flock: seven days it shall be with its mother; on eighth day you shall give it to me.

familiar.text: Likewise shalt thou do with thine oxen, and with thy sheep: seven days it shall be with his dam; on the eighth day thou shalt give it me.

verses.restored: You shall be holy people to me; flesh torn in field you shall not eat; to dog you shall throw it.

familiar.text: And ye shall be holy men unto me: neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs.

translation_notes: Restitution dominates property injury/theft material: harm requires repair, often more than replacement.
Seduction/bride-price laws are patriarchal and require ethical audit; preserve source but do not present as modern sexual ethics.
Verses 18-20 contain severe holiness prohibitions and require reception-history safeguards, especially around accusations of sorcery.
Sojourner/widow/orphan/poor protections are central: Israel's memory of Egypt becomes anti-oppression law.
No interest on poor and returning cloak before night protect survival dignity.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter to justify violence against accused witches, sexual coercion, patriarchy, or harsh debt practice. The restored layer preserves ancient law; ethical application must be governed by anti-oppression, protection of vulnerable people, and liberation memory.
